content: 1. Elagolix reduces the levels or effects of encorafenib by altering the metabolism mediated by the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored. Elagolix is a weak-to-moderate inducer of CYP3A4. If co-administered, monitor CYP3A substrates and consider increasing their dose if necessary. 2. Elagolix reduces the levels or effects of entrectinib by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy adjustments or close monitoring are recommended. Elagolix acts as a weak-to-moderate CYP3A4 inducer. Monitor CYP3A substrates during co-administration and adjust their dose as needed. 3. Enzalutamide decreases the levels or effects of elagolix by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism. Conversely, elagolix reduces the levels or effects of enzalutamide through the same mechanism. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored. Elagolix is a weak-to-moderate CYP3A4 inducer. Monitor CYP3A substrates if co-administered and consider dose adjustments. 4. Elagolix reduces the levels or effects of eplerenone by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy adjustments or close monitoring are advised. Elagolix is a weak-to-moderate CYP3A4 inducer. Monitor CYP3A substrates during co-administration and adjust their dose if necessary. 5.
